caveats: The grounded procedure calls for tximport with type='rsem' so that RSEM effective lengths enter the model as an offset. Those per-sample files were not delivered, so this step deviates: rounding a pre-summarized expected-count matrix. Genes whose effective length differs systematically between samples can be biased by this, and the report must say so rather than imply the reference path was followed.
sample_01's low depth is handled by its size factor; it widens that sample's contribution uncertainty rather than biasing fold changes. Do not drop it in the primary fit.
At 6 replicates per group DESeq2 flags rather than replaces count outliers, so some genes will legitimately carry NA p-values.

steps.description: Fit the differential expression model on the 12,000 x 12 RSEM count matrix. Pre-filter minimally: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Set the condition factor's reference level explicitly to the control level as named in metadata.csv — do not rely on alphabetical ordering — and name the contrast as the triple (condition, treated, control) so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Fit DESeq2 with median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, run the Wald test, keep Cook's-distance outlier flagging on (at 6 replicates per cell DESeq2 sets the p-value to NA rather than replacing the count) and report how many genes got an NA p-value from the outlier flag separately from those removed by independent filtering. Plot the histogram of unadjusted p-values before adjustment and describe its shape. Apply BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha = 0.05 and shrink the log2 fold changes with apeglm for the condition coefficient, keeping the unshrunken estimate and its standard error in the table. Write the full results table (gene symbol, baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue, padj) and the significant subset. Finally, re-run the same pipeline with sample_01 excluded and report how many significant genes are gained and lost — as a sensitivity check only, with the full 12-sample fit remaining the primary result.

plan.title: Colon treated vs control DE from RSEM counts
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level RSEM expected-count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 human colon samples, counts.csv) with a metadata table (metadata.csv) giving one condition per sample: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. The research question is purely 'which genes differ between treated and control', so the plan stops at differential expression plus its diagnostics — no enrichment step is added, since that is scope the question did not ask for.

Two data facts drive the design. First, the matrix holds RSEM expected counts, which are not integers, and the per-sample genes.results files carrying the effective lengths were not delivered. The grounded procedure (R-0065) wants tximport with type='rsem' so the effective lengths enter the model as an offset; that path is unavailable here because only the summarized matrix exists. T1S2 therefore documents the deviation explicitly, rounds the expected counts to integers for DESeq2 (the only remaining option for a pre-summarized RSEM matrix), and states in its output that no length offset was applied — this matters for genes whose effective length shifts between samples, and the step must say so rather than pretend it followed the reference path. If the genes.results files can be supplied later, the analysis should be re-run through tximport.

Second, sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median. Per R-0008/R-0030 it is kept, not silently dropped: T1S1 reports its library size and detected-gene count beside the other 11, places it on the blind-VST PCA and the sample-distance heatmap, and the median-of-ratios size factors absorb the depth difference inside the negative binomial model. Removal would require a stated reason from the QC, and depth alone is not one. T1S2 additionally reports a leave-one-out sensitivity check without sample_01 so the reader can see whether any call depends on that single shallow library.

T1S1 (QC) -> T1S2 (filter, model, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH) -> T1S3 (edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check and the final report). T1S3 runs the second method on the same counts and the same design and reports the intersection as the high-confidence set, which R-0042 recommends precisely at 6 replicates per group where the two tools begin to diverge. The dataset is tiny (12,000 x 12), so every step is cheap.

Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples
~ condition with explicit reference level control; RSEM expected counts rounded with stated caveat because per-sample genes.results with effective lengths were not delivered
Overlap of DESeq2 Wald and edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness check; MA and dispersion plots; session info
